title: Pinch-pot elongated olive dish
subtitle: A shallow oval dish for olives or nibbles, built from a single pinched ball
excerpt: An elongated olive dish starts as a standard pinch pot then gets pulled gently into an oval by pressing the rim from opposite sides. The result is a shallow, low-sided dish, 18-20 cm at the longest point, that sits flat on the table and holds olives or small snacks. No kiln needed.
sourceNotes: Pinch-pot forming derived from first principles. Elongated dish forms appear throughout the historical pottery record from Roman to mediaeval European domestic ware.

glossaryTerms.definition: A vessel formed by pressing the thumb into a ball of clay and pinching the walls outward between thumb and fingers
The stage at which the clay holds its shape but is still cool and slightly flexible , the best moment for refining the form
Fully air-dried; pale and lightweight, ready for sealing

content.text: A
pinch pot

pulled into an oval makes a low, stable olive dish with walls just high enough to keep contents on the table. This version uses air-dry clay , the oval is set at leather-hard stage and the whole piece dries without a kiln. The base is kept flat so the dish does not rock.

materials.name: PVA glue diluted 50/50 with water (for sealing)

content.text: Forming the pinch pot
Wedge 200 g of air-dry clay into a smooth ball with no cracks or air pockets.

Press your thumb into the centre of the ball, stopping 1 cm from the base. Rotate the ball and pinch the wall between your thumb on the inside and your index finger on the outside, working up the wall in small increments. Target a wall thickness of 7-8 mm throughout.
Continue pinching until the base is flat and the walls are about 4 cm high. The rim should be a gentle, consistent curve about 16 cm in diameter at this stage.
Place the bowl upside down on a flat surface for five minutes to flatten the base. Then turn it right side up.
Pulling the oval

While the clay is still soft, place both palms flat against opposite sides of the rim. Press inward gently on both sides simultaneously , this pushes the rim outward in the other direction, converting the circle to an oval.
Work slowly, pressing a little at a time. The target is an oval roughly 20 cm at the long axis and 13 cm at the short axis.
Smooth the inside of the dish with a damp wooden rib, working from the centre outward.
Drying and setting the shape
Set the dish on a flat board. Allow it to reach
leather-hard

, roughly two to four hours in a normal room , then refine the rim and base if needed. Compress the rim gently with a damp sponge to round any sharp edges. Check the base by setting the dish on a flat tile; trim any high spots with a needle tool. Leave uncovered to finish drying to
bone-dry
Sealing

Apply two coats of diluted PVA to all surfaces. Once sealed, the dish can be wiped clean. Air-dry clay is not food-safe without a tested glaze. Olives and dry snacks in a bowl liner work fine; do not put the dish in water or fill it with liquid.
Variations
Score a simple line pattern around the outside wall with a needle tool at leather-hard for decoration.
Make three smaller versions , 10 cm oval , as a matched condiment set.
Add a small pinched spout at one end by pulling the rim forward before the clay stiffens.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Rim cracked when pulling the oval
items.cause: The clay had already stiffened too much , the rim was past the soft working stage
items.fix: Work faster next time while the clay is still soft. If cracks have appeared, dampen with a sponge, smooth closed, and allow to stiffen before touching again

items.problem: Base rocks on a flat surface
items.cause: The base was not flattened by pressing on a flat surface while the clay was soft
items.fix: At leather-hard, press the base down firmly on a flat tile. If fully dry, carefully sand the base on fine sandpaper in circular strokes

items.problem: Walls too thin in one area, thick in another
items.cause: Uneven pinching , too many rotations on one side
items.fix: At leather-hard, gently press the thicker areas inward to redistribute. Thin spots are harder to fix; add a small patch of clay with slip and blend if thin spots feel fragile
